title: Information register and periodicity
goal: Choose rate-register dimensions, resource and periodicity and verify a price as of a date.
prerequisites: onec.p5; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Choose rate-register dimensions, resource and periodicity and verify a price as of a date.
sections: An information register suits rates by service and time. Service is a dimension, rate a resource, and period adds history. An attribute stores extra description rather than replacing the key. Start from “which rate applied toS1 atD”; one current card price cannot answer the historical question.

Choose a register from the data question. “Which rate applied?” needs keyed temporal state;“how much was delivered this week?” needs turnover;“what obligation remains?” needs balance. Similar-looking fields do not imply equal mechanisms or invariants. Write a small independent example for each and explain why another register type would answer the wrong question.

Two records for one service in one period follow the key policy. Daily periodicity cannot distinguish two intraday changes under the same key. Do not substitute current time just to bypass a collision. Choose required precision and test exactly at a rate-change boundary.

Dimensions define slices, resources measured quantities, and recorders provenance where supported. Adding a dimension changes keys and granularity:customer totals may split by service. Define old-data treatment and grand-total reconciliation before restructuring. New granularity is more than another displayed column; it changes writes, uniqueness and the interpretation of historical records.
A slice is not a sum of prices

Between changes, use the latest applicable rate rather than summing history. SliceLast represents state at a time; record sets represent history. Explicitly return absence or reject when no prior rate exists. Automatic zero can resemble a free service and hide missing data.

Time boundaries belong in specifications. State uses an as-of moment, turnover an interval, and movements an agreed period. Test before the first fact, exactly at a change and after it. Equal totals without matching identities do not prove correctness:errors for different customers can cancel numerically while allocations remain wrong.

Set rate 100 fromD1 and 150 fromD2. Expect absence beforeD1, 100 betweenD1/D2, and 150 at the agreed inclusiveD2 boundary. Reopen and verify. Repeating the same keys must not increase count; editing copy rates must preserve the source.

Trace totals back to original facts. Preserve recorder-level records, independent arithmetic and reversal results. Reposting one document must not affect unrelated sets. For accounting models, test both side equality and analytic meaning. Array exercises demonstrate algorithms but do not replace actual execution of the corresponding platform mechanism. Record that distinction in the evidence and acceptance scope.
